text:
Aisha (CS): heads-up: AcmePay reports intermittent 403s when they send a mixed batch that asks for an embedding + a generation in the same request. They say embeddings-only calls succeed. Customer says the key was created via SSO provisioning 

AcmePay (customer): "we're seeing failures ~3% of requests, always 403. example: curl to /v1/batch that requests embeddings for doc and generation for summary — the server returns insufficient_scope. we can't repro locally with our personal keys." :frowning:

Kiran (Infra): can you paste a redacted request + response? also need the api key prefix (first 8 chars) and org id so I can grep logs.

Aisha (CS): paste below (key masked):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/batch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ABCD1234xxxxxxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "requests": [
      {"type": "embedding", "model": "rwd-embed-1", "input": "invoice text"},
      {"type": "generation", "model": "rwd-gen-1", "prompt": "summarize invoice"}
    ]
  }'
```

Response (customer):

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient_scope",
    "message": "API key lacks 'generation' permission",
    "code": 403
  }
}
```

Aisha (CS): key prefix is sk-ABCD1234, org=acmepay-org-77. they said the org admin used SSO auto-provisioner to create a service key and selected scopes "embeddings, rerank" in their portal (no generation).

Sophie (Solutions): this matches a known footgun: if a key is missing generation scope and a single batch contains both embeddings + generation, the platform validates required scopes for the whole multi-op request and rejects when any op needs a scope that's not present. embedding-only calls succeed which explains the intermittent nature when some clients split requests.

Kiran (Infra): i'm seeing corresponding logs for sk-ABCD1234 (masked) in infra logs: infra-bot attached an abbreviated trace: 

infra-bot: ``[1967778892] request_id=rx-9f3a status=403 org=acmepay-org-77 error="insufficient_scope: missing generation" route=/v1/batch``

Kiran (Infra): checked provisioning audit — the SSO provisioner created the key with scopes ["embeddings","rerank"]. generation missing. looks like SCIM template omitted generation for service keys by default.

Aisha (CS): customer says they didn't intend to omit generation, but SSO admin flow is locked down and they can't re-provision immediately due to approvals. they want a temporary workaround while they coordinate with their identity team.

Sophie (Solutions): workarounds (ordered):
1) ask them to split their client: send embeddings and generation as separate calls using the same key — generation call will 403 unless the key has generation scope, so this only helps if some requests can avoid generation. not ideal.
2) create a short-lived admin API key (if they have an org owner who can do this) that includes generation and hand it to the app config for a controlled window.
3) we can create a scoped proxy token on our side (requires approval) that maps to generation-only and returns a token for their service — needs SRE sign-off (security).

Jonah (Support Manager): escalate this as P2 until customer confirms workaround. need timeline: can they get admin approval within 48h? also ask Security whether we can mint a temporary bridging token.

Aisha (CS): customer says approvals will take 2-3 business days. they asked if Redwood can help identify which provisioning policy created the key and whether it's possible to auto-add generation to service keys.

Kiran (Infra): opened an internal ticket to fix SCIM templates: looks like template "servicekey-defaults-v2" excludes generation for keys created via SSO. tagging @SRE for security review. attaching audit entries: devops-bot uploaded 2 entries: 

devops-bot: https://internal.redwood/ops/audit/acmepay-org-77/keys/evt-98765 (scim:create)

Sophie (Solutions): immediate operational fix we can do (requires approvals): manually patch the key scopes in the admin UI/DB to add "generation" for sk-ABCD1234. steps for ops: 

1) verify key ownership via org metadata (org id acmepay-org-77)
2) patch scopes via admin API: 

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://console.redwood.ai/internal/orgs/acmepay-org-77/keys/sk-ABCD1234 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"scopes": ["embeddings","rerank","generation"]}'
```

3) confirm via key list and ask customer to retry.

Kiran (Infra): NOTE: manual patch will be audited and requires a ticket + approval. security wants to review the request to ensure no policy violations. I'll start the ticket and add the approval chain.

Jonah (Support Manager): please add the customer-facing message template so Aisha can share with AcmePay: explain cause, mitigation, and ETA for SCIM template fix. include recommended short-term workaround and request org-owner approval for scope patch.

Aisha (CS): drafting message now, will send after ops confirms ticket.

AcmePay (customer): thanks for the quick triage. curious if other customers hit this or if it's specific to our SCIM setup.

Kiran (Infra): we've seen a handful of other reports where service-account provisioning omitted generation — recorded two internal incidents last quarter. patching SCIM template will be a global fix; i put it on the infra backlog and linked this ticket.

Sophie (Solutions): action items: 
- Kiran: open ops change ticket + ask Security for expedited approval to patch sk-ABCD1234 (include org ownership verification).
- Jonah/Aisha: share the short-term guidance with customer and collect confirmation that they approve the manual patch if required.
- Infra: roll SCIM template fix and add guardrails in the SSO UI to warn when generation is unchecked for service keys.

Aisha (CS): ack, will update customer and post back. :thumbsup:

devops-bot: ticket created -> OPS-4521 (manual scope patch request) by kiran. assigned to security-review.

Kiran (Infra): leaving notes for whoever picks the OPS ticket: ensure DB write goes through the admin service (not direct DB) so audit triggers and rotation hooks run. also rotate key if customer requests after patch.

Sophie (Solutions): adding a long-term suggestion: when we validate batch requests, we could return a more actionable error payload that lists which scopes are missing (e.g., {"missing_scopes":["generation"]}) to make client UX clearer. logged as FE-827.

Aisha (CS): closing loop for now — will update thread after customer confirms approval.

(THREAD END)
